title: NYC Street Flow: project outcome scorecards
author: Samuel Webber
status: Evidence inventory, not identified causal effects

definitions.flow: People crossing a fixed boundary per hour, direction and aligned time interval
definitions.time: Mean minutes for comparable complete journeys, including access, waits and transfers
definitions.minutes: Sum of complete journey minutes, reported alongside trip totals; separate fixed-composition and actual-mix measures

projects.name: Prospect Park West
projects.subtitle: 2010 · three moving lanes → two

flow.detail: Evening street-count scenario after separately accounting for the B69. Requires stable 1.3-person non-B69 motor occupancy and transferred historical bus loads. This range is not a confidence interval.

time.detail: Measured driving segment: controlled changes from −36 to +11 seconds across comparison streets, 7 a.m.–7 p.m. Only two weekdays before and two after; these do not represent every traveler’s trip.

minutes.detail: No contemporaneous traveler weights or complete journey times for the affected network. Hypothetical fixed-drive totals remain scenarios.

blockers: Bicycle and vehicle observations use different sites and dates.
B69 relocation changes passenger flow on PPW and nearby streets.
Parallel streets had concurrent changes; the comparison cannot isolate the lane.
projects.next: Obtain retained synchronized passenger counts and B69 load/reroute records. If these were never collected, retain the conditional result rather than filling the gap with assumed riders.
links: DOT raw counts and timed runs

projects.name: Third Avenue
projects.subtitle: 2023 · combined bus, bike and street redesign

flow.detail: Motor occupants + bus riders at E60th Street, 2022→2024, 16:00–19:00. Source occupancy estimates are included. Cycling is observed at E50th, outside the project; walking is missing at the motor boundary.

time.detail: Measured bus segment: −28 seconds relative to Lexington, while the pre-period placebo is +52 seconds. Run-weighted time over E67th–E97th is not passenger-weighted door-to-door time.

minutes.detail: Bus runs cannot supply passenger-minutes without segment loads. Add access, waits, transfers and other modes before evaluating the complete network.

blockers: Bus and bike lanes, intersection work and signal changes form one package.
The primary comparison fails a reassuring pre-period stability check.
Motor and bicycle counts do not share a boundary; bus onboard loads remain missing.
Route-level bus fare entries were already falling against other Upper East Side routes before construction, so they cannot show a package effect either.
projects.next: Use staged DOT and MTA records to verify treatment dates, timepoint continuity, bus loads and an eligible longer comparison history. Estimate the combined redesign unless its components can be separated.

projects.name: Pulaski / McGuinness approach
projects.subtitle: 2015–16 construction · detector and bridge are different locations

flow.detail: Continuous directional vehicle counts at station 021284 support motor-volume comparisons. Occupancy, aligned bicycle counts and the bridge screenline are not supplied by that detector.

time.detail: A motor-count record contains no elapsed journey time. Available Citi Bike records cannot reconstruct every private-bike, motor or transit traveler’s door-to-door trip.

minutes.detail: Neither all-mode traveler weights nor complete time observations are aligned to a verified permanent lane-closure date.

blockers: Junctions between the detector and Pulaski Bridge allow entries, exits and diversion.
Permanent motor-lane closure timing and detector continuity need agency confirmation.
The automatic bridge bicycle series begins after conversion; the Bronx donor roads have incomplete common coverage.
projects.next: Verify station coordinates, direction codes, lane channels and quality logs before treating the motor series as continuous. Use shared calendar cells and present each direction separately.

projects.name: Brooklyn Bridge
projects.subtitle: 2021 · Manhattan-bound moving lane → two-way bikeway

flow.detail: Representative evening profile, 2018→2024, both directions: motor occupants, cyclists and pedestrians. Motor occupancy is estimated by the source; the mode surveys are not synchronized.

time.detail: Fixed-station Citi Bike trips and borough-level commute surveys supply separate context. They do not follow the same affected travelers before and after the conversion.

minutes.detail: Survey-weighted usual-commute minutes can describe the borough pair. A changing number and mix of commuters prevents interpreting their total as daily minutes saved by the lane.

blockers: The intervention coincides with pandemic-era commuting changes.
Neighboring bridges can receive diverted travelers and have different pre-trends.
Subway, tunnel and ferry totals broaden the boundary but do not identify individual switches.
projects.next: Keep bridge, three-bridge and wider sector boundaries visible. Obtain aligned modal dates and a credible comparison design; do not infer a driver→subway transition from aggregate ridership changes.

projects.name: Tenth / Amsterdam Avenue
projects.subtitle: 2019 · full-time moving lane → protected bikeway

flow.detail: Northbound motor occupants + bus riders at W60th Street, 2018→2019, 16:00–19:00. The first comparison predates the pandemic. Aligned cycling and walking at this crossing are absent.

time.detail: No matched all-mode complete journey panel establishes travel time changes caused by this conversion.

minutes.detail: The motor-and-bus subtotal cannot be multiplied by an unrelated citywide or modal average to produce a defensible network time burden.

blockers: Cycling is counted at W50th Street, south of the original project section.
Walking at the motor boundary and comparable whole trips are missing.
Later comparisons add pandemic changes and a 2023 bikeway extension through the bicycle count site.
projects.next: Prioritize the 2018→2019 window, verify count dates and obtain a comparable untreated corridor. Add contemporaneous cycling and walking at W60th before reporting all-mode flow.
